subject: Invoice line-item normalization request after marketplace cutover
body:
From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmeapps.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: May invoice looks doubled for some marketplace SKUs

Jordan,

Hope you are well. Our finance team just pulled the May invoice that came through the AWS marketplace and noticed duplicated line items for two SKU groups: API-usage-standard and API-usage-eu. The total shows a 62% increase vs expected consumption, but our usage export shows only ~15% growth. I attached the invoice and our CSV extract.

Files attached: acme_may_invoice.pdf, acme_usage_may.csv

Can you help confirm whether this is a platform metering cutover issue or a billing replication on your side? We need to resolve before our month-end close.

Thanks,
Lisa Chen
Finance Director, Acme Apps
---

On Sat, May 9, 2027 at 10:05 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmeapps.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 May 2027 10:05:32 -0700
Subject: Re: May invoice looks doubled for some marketplace SKUs

Lisa,

Thanks for flagging this and for the attachments. Sorry for the trouble during your close. We recently completed a marketplace metering cutover for several SKUs on May 1st that consolidated some internal meter IDs. It sounds like the invoice line normalization did not correctly collapse legacy meter entries.

Immediate next steps from our side: 
- Marissa will run a reconciliation of the CSV you provided vs our server-side meter exports and produce a delta file.
- I will open an expedited billing case with AWS and GCP (ccing their billing contacts below) and request a corrected invoice or an offset credit.
- Rishi, please confirm any VAT/tax implications if we apply a retroactive credit for May.

Timeline target: initial analysis by Tue 11 May, proposed credit/adjusted invoice by Fri 14 May. I will keep you updated daily until resolved.

Attachments: redwood_internal_analysis_may12.xlsx (provisional)

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmeapps.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: May invoice looks doubled for some marketplace SKUs - initial findings

Jordan / Lisa,

I pulled a quick reconciliation. Key findings from the acme_usage_may.csv vs our internal meter export: 
- There are duplicate meter_id values that map to both legacy-MTR-201 and new-MTR-501 for API-usage-standard. Both meters were billed separately due to incomplete normalization on the marketplace ingest.
- For API-usage-eu we see the same pattern plus one negative adjustment line (adj-RTN-03) applied to a previous period that seems to have reflowed into May.
- Total duplicated amount on the invoice ~ $48,700; expected legitimate net increase ~ $9,300.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Create one consolidated usage CSV with normalized meter mapping and attach as evidence to the marketplace ticket.
2) Request provisional credit equal to the duplicated amount while AWS/GCP issue corrected invoice.
3) Hold off on tax/VAT treatment until Rishi confirms the correct crediting mechanism.

I uploaded a reconciliation tab to the shared sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1example (readonly link provided to Lisa).

Marissa
Marketplace Billing Lead, Redwood Inference
---

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: AWS Marketplace Billing <billing@amazonaws.com>, GCP Marketplace Support <marketplace-support@google.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmeapps.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: URGENT: Incorrect invoice line-item duplication after metering cutover - Acme Apps (ACM-2026-037)

Hello,

We believe there is an invoice line-item duplication for customer Acme Apps (account id ACM-2026-037) following a marketplace metering cutover completed May 1. Attached are: acme_may_invoice.pdf, acme_usage_may.csv, and our normalized usage CSV and reconciliation workbook. 

Requested actions: 
- Please confirm whether your ingest normalized legacy meter IDs into a single billable meter, or if legacy and new meter IDs were billed separately.
- If separate, please open a ticket to correct the May invoice and issue an offsetting credit. We request a provisional credit for $48,700 while you review.
- Provide the support case number and expected timing.

Customer impact: Acme is going through month-end close and needs the corrected invoice or an offset to avoid manual accruals.

Thank you,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---

From: AWS Marketplace Billing <billing@amazonaws.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2027 12:04:15 -0700
Subject: Re: URGENT: Incorrect invoice line-item duplication after metering cutover - Acme Apps (ACM-2026-037)

Hello Jordan,

Thank you for the information and attachments. We have created support case AWS-CASE-20270512-8876. To expedite, please provide the following: a sample of the raw meter IDs from your normalized CSV (first 100 rows), and the account marketplace buyer id. Once we have those items we will triage whether the duplication occurred during our ingest or from the provider-side submission. Estimated initial response within 48 hours.

Regards,
AWS Marketplace Billing Support
---

On Thu, May 13, 2027 at 15:40 Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmeapps.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, AWS Marketplace Billing <billing@amazonaws.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: May invoice looks doubled for some marketplace SKUs - plan and provisional credit

Lisa,

Quick update: AWS acknowledged and opened case AWS-CASE-20270512-8876. They requested the normalized sample and buyer id; Marissa has uploaded the sample to the support case and shared the buyer id in the case notes.

To reduce your month-end noise, Redwood will apply a provisional internal credit for $48,700 to your account the week of May 17. This is a temporary measure while AWS/GCP investigate and issue any formal invoice adjustments. Once the marketplace provides either a corrected invoice or a documented denial, we will reconcile the provisional credit and issue any necessary tax documentation.

Action items: 
- Marissa: confirm sample uploaded and post support case link in HubSpot.
- Rishi: confirm VAT treatment for a provisional credit vs an invoiced correction; we need guidance before issuing credit memo.
- Lisa: confirm you are comfortable receiving a provisional credit and we will adjust if marketplace issues a different outcome.

Thanks for your patience, we aim to close this by next Friday.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachments referenced above are retained in thread: acme_may_invoice.pdf (PDF), acme_usage_may.csv (CSV), redwood_internal_analysis_may12.xlsx (XLSX)]
